title: The Residue on the Far Side — Gunshot Propellant Grains Near an Exit Wound, Ballistic Composite Wound-Channel Transport, Secondary Transfer & SEM-EDS

teenKit.tldr: Textbooks claim unburned gunpowder can only stick to the entrance of a gunshot wound, but real-world cases and physics models show debris can travel completely through a human body to the exit wound.
teenKit.whyItMatters: This case proves that real life is far messier than textbook rules, showing how fragile physical evidence is and how easily investigators can misinterpret anomalies as frame-jobs or contamination.
keyTakeaways: Unburned propellant flakes traditionally signal a bullet's entry point, making their sudden appearance at an exit wound a major forensic puzzle.
Composite transport models reveal that skin, muscle, and bone can trap and carry microscopic debris all the way through a wound channel.
When physical evidence like green gunpowder flakes gets lost during transport, a single photograph can become the only proof an anomaly ever existed.

vocab.meaning: Tiny particles of burned and unburned propellant and primer materials left behind when a firearm is discharged.
The opening where a projectile leaves the body, typically displaying different tearing patterns than an entrance wound.
A simulation using layers like skin, gelatin, and bone to study how physical materials move and behave inside a body.
A high-tech microscopy and elemental analysis tool used to identify the exact chemical composition of microscopic particles.

quiz.question: According to traditional ballistics rules, where should unburned gunpowder flakes be found?
options: Floating in the air near the shooter
quiz.explanation: Textbook rules dictate that unburned propellant blasts forward out of the barrel and gets caught on the very first thing in its path—the entry point.

quiz.question: What made the forensic investigation particularly terrifying in Weber et al.'s case?
options: The physical gunpowder flakes vanished during transport, leaving only a photograph
quiz.explanation: The actual physical flakes were lost during transport, meaning investigators had to rely solely on a single contemporaneous photograph.

quiz.question: What is the primary function of SEM-EDS in forensic analysis?
options: Measuring the velocity of a bullet
Analyzing the elemental particle classification of microscopic residue
quiz.explanation: SEM-EDS combines scanning electron microscopy with elemental analysis to accurately classify the chemical makeup of tiny residue particles.
